questions.question: Which organisms lack a membrane-bound nucleus?
choices: Fungi
Protists with nuclei
Bacteria
Animals

questions.question: Which group includes yeast?
choices: Fungi
Viruses
Bacteria
Archaea

questions.question: Which description best fits a virus?
choices: A prokaryotic cell that divides by binary fission
A eukaryotic cell that carries out independent metabolism
A multicellular organism that reproduces through spores
A noncellular agent that reproduces using host machinery

questions.question: Which feature is characteristic of a bacteriophage?
choices: It is a bacterial organelle
It infects bacteria
It reproduces only in plants
It contains no genetic material

questions.question: What is binary fission?
choices: Fusion of two gametes
Division of one prokaryotic cell into two cells
Assembly of a virus outside all cells
Formation of a fungal fruiting body

questions.question: What is a pathogen?
choices: An organism that always improves host health
A community of microbes in one habitat
A chemical messenger produced by nerve cells
An agent capable of causing disease

questions.question: What is a microbiome?
choices: A community of microorganisms in a particular environment
The genetic material of one microorganism
A particular habitat's nonliving conditions
A group containing only disease-causing viruses

questions.question: Why are not all microorganisms harmful?
choices: Disease-causing and beneficial microbes have identical ecological roles
Only multicellular organisms recycle nutrients
Many support processes such as decomposition or nutrient cycling
All microbial interactions reduce other organisms' survival

questions.question: Why can bacteria reproduce without a host cell while viruses cannot reproduce independently?
choices: Viruses contain the same complete cellular machinery as bacteria
Bacteria reproduce only inside the same hosts as viruses
Viruses obtain all energy through independent photosynthesis
Bacteria have cellular machinery; viruses rely on host machinery

questions.question: How can microbes contribute to nitrogen cycling?
choices: All microbes perform the same nitrogen transformation
Some transform nitrogen into forms other organisms can use
Only plant roots can transform atmospheric nitrogen
Microbes use nitrogen but cannot change its chemical form

questions.question: Why does yeast cause bread dough to rise?
choices: It produces oxygen while consuming carbon dioxide
It releases nitrogen by breaking down flour proteins
It releases carbon dioxide during sugar metabolism
It traps air without any contribution from metabolism

questions.question: Why can decomposer microorganisms affect soil fertility?
choices: They break down material and return nutrients to usable pools
They store all released nutrients where plants cannot use them
They slow every chemical process in soil
They consume organic matter without returning any nutrients

questions.question: What helps explain why viruses are often described as noncellular?
choices: They lack a complete cellular organization and independent metabolism
They have no physical structure
They always contain a nucleus
They reproduce through ordinary mitosis

questions.question: How do bacterial spores differ from typical reproductive spores of many fungi?
choices: Both always double bacterial population size
Fungal spores cannot germinate
Many bacterial endospores are survival structures rather than new offspring
Bacterial endospores are viruses

questions.question: Why must a culture experiment use approved containment and procedures?
choices: Containment is needed only for visibly large organisms
Unknown microorganisms can present risks
An unknown culture can be treated as harmless until illness occurs
Handling procedures cannot influence exposure to microbes

questions.question: An observed cell has a nucleus and chloroplasts and lives independently in water. Which classification is plausible?
choices: A bacteriophage
A bacterial endospore
A virus
A photosynthetic protist

questions.question: A sample's agent multiplies only inside host cells and lacks ribosomes. Which group best fits?
choices: Bacteria
Yeasts
Viruses
Single-celled protists

questions.question: In a teacher-controlled investigation, a sealed sterile medium shows no growth while an otherwise comparable exposed medium shows growth. What is supported?
choices: Every organism in the exposed sample causes disease
The sterile sample proves all air contains no microbes
The comparison identifies the exact species present
Exposure introduced organisms capable of growing in the medium

questions.question: A community contains decomposing fungi and nitrogen-fixing bacteria. What do these roles illustrate?
choices: Microbes performing only one ecological function
Microbial participation in nutrient cycling
Every microorganism acting as a producer
Nutrient cycling occurring independently of organisms
